---- Respondents (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Awadh Tripathi, Advocate For Stae/Respondent : Mr. Shailendra Sharma, Panel Lawyer For Respondent
No.2 : None Hon'ble Shri Justice Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice Hon'ble Shri Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad, J Order on Board Per Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice 04/12/2024 1.
The Heard, Mr. Awadh Tripathi, learned counsel for the petitioners as well as Mr. Shailendra Sharma, learned Panel Lawyer for the State.

None appears on behalf of respondent No.2.
2.

Both the petitions have been filed by the petitioners with the same prayer as quoted below :
"It is, therefore, prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to allow the petition and quash the FIR at Mahila Thana Raipur with Crime No.38/2024 registered offence under 498-A, 34 in the interest of justice."

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners in both the petitions submits that on 18.11.2024, this Court referred the present matter for the Mediation Centre of this Court, and on the date of hearing i.e. on 29.11.2024, the matter has been amicably settled between both the parties before the Mediator with the various terms and conditions of both the parties.

4. As per report dated 28.11.2024 whereby the parties have arrived at compromise and entered into SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT vide Mediation R. No. M/267 & 268/2024, dated 28.11.2024, in CRMP No.1891/2024 (Dinesh Mangal & Others vs. State of Chhattisgarh & another) link with CRMP No.2012/2024 (Anurag Mangal vs. State of Chhattisgarh & another) and also considering their rival submissions made hereinabove and also went through the records with utmost circumspection wherein the agreement is signed on 28.11.2024 by the parties to the agreement in the presence of Mediator at Mediation Centre, High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh and the copies of SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT are being handed-over to both the parties, nothing survives to be adjudicated.
5. From Office note dated 29.11.2024, it is evident that the Mediator after conducting mediation sessions has informed vide report dated 28.11.2024 that:
"Shri Anurag Mangal present.
Smt. Agrima Goyal present.

In view of the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners in both the cases and the compromise entered between the parties, which is evident from the Office note dated Dinesh Kumar Mangal vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146211820/
2 29.11.2024, in which report of mediation dated 28.11.2024 is annexed, both the petitions are allowed and the FIR bearing Crime No. 38 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Mahila Thana,
District Raipur (C.G.) dated 21.02.2024 for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 34 of the IPC against the petitioners are hereby quashed subject to the condition that the petitioners shall comply with the terms and conditions of the settlement arrived at between the parties before the Mediation Centre of this Court dated 28.11.2024.
 Sd/- Sd/-
 (Amitendra Kishore Prasad) (Ramesh Sinha)
